questions.question: What should you do if a driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Flash your brake lights before slowing down to warn the other driver.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake lights before slowing down to warn the other driver.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake lights before slowing down. This warns the tailgater. The other driver may not see hazards ahead that require slowing down.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips. These trips are usually less than 5 miles long and at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: What group formation is best for riding in curves or entering a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use a single-file line when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway. This is safer than other formations in these situations.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip from car drippings. Is this safe for motorcycles?

options.text: No, it is never safe for motorcycles.
No, you should always avoid it since other parts of the lane are safer.
Yes, it improves traction for motorcycle tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of the lane. When the road is dry, this area usually has enough grip for safe riding. The oily strip is usually only about 2 feet wide, so you can ride to one side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle for best control?

options.text: With your arms fully stretched out.
Using your arms to hold your body up.
Keeping your knees away from the gas tank.
Keeping your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your arms should bend slightly when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: What should you do if the throttle gets stuck?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: Twist the throttle back and forth to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down at first, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down at first, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then speed up and leave it behind. If you see a larger animal, brake and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Where should less experienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they won't have to chase the group. More experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What is the best way to ride in the rain?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from cars hasn't washed away yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: How do you stop a motorcycle as quickly as possible in a straight line?

options.text: Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: The best way to stop quickly is to use both the front and rear brakes at the same time. Do not lock either wheel. Always use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle and car crashes happen because a car driver fails to give the motorcycle the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle and car crashes happen because a car driver fails to give the motorcycle the right-of-way.

questions.question: What is the best way to make sure other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Weave back and forth in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and position your motorcycle where other drivers can easily see you. Keep a safe distance between you and other vehicles so you can react if needed. Do not assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Squeeze the front brake hard to prevent the tire from locking.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake gently to avoid locking the wheel. Apply light pressure to the rear brake as well.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes with short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on surfaces. Tuck in any loose laces so they cannot get caught on anything.

questions.question: What should a rider do when making a slow, tight turn?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean away from the turn direction.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean with your motorcycle. However, in slow, tight turns, keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.

questions.question: Is there a part of the lane you should always avoid?

options.text: No, there is no part that should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, there is no part that should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position that is always best, and no single lane position that should always be avoided. Choose your lane position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle rider position themselves in their lane?

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no one best lane position and no position to always avoid. Adjust your position based on changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are about to slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are about to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is following you too closely, flash your brake light before you start to slow down. The driver behind you may not see hazards ahead that you are slowing to avoid.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily buildup. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid it when the road is wet.
Ride on it because it has better traction.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Do not worry about oil in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid it when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars and trucks build up in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this strip usually still has enough traction for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride beside it and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead the group.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of the lane when passing. This helps you see oncoming traffic better and makes you more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Try to get onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on either side of the lane is more dangerous and may cause the passing driver to cut back into your lane too early.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required for effective eye or face shield protection?

options.text: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
Able to allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
questions.explanation: Effective eye or face shields must be free of scratches, fasten securely, allow clear side views, prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed. They should NOT be too tight.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.
